Name of the Event : CUBE CRAZE

 

Type of Event (Onstage / Offstage) : OFFSTAGE

 

Number of Participants: 2

 

Number of Rounds: 3

 

Rules and Regulations / Guidelines:

 

Game Setup

 

• Participants will compete in teams of two.

• Every team will receive one Rubik's Cube with the same predetermined scramble.

• One teammate will be the Director, and the other will be the Solver.

• The Solver must wear a blindfold throughout Rounds 1 and 2.

• If the Solver removes the blindfold at any time during these rounds, the team will be disqualified.

• Team members cannot switch roles during the competition. The Director must remain the Director, and the Solver must remain the Solver.

• Once the cube is solved, the Solver must place the cube on the table to stop the timer.

• The competition consists of three rounds.

 



 

Round 1 – Verbal Guidance Round

 

How to Play

 

• The Director may look at the cube.

• The Director must verbally guide the blindfolded Solver to solve the cube.

• The Director must not touch the cube at any time.

• The Solver may act only on the Director's verbal instructions.

• Each team will have 15 minutes to solve the cube.

• Teams that do not solve the cube within the time limit will be eliminated.

• The top 5 teams with the shortest solving times will advance to Round 2.

 



 

Round 2 – Opposite Direction Round

 

How to Play

 

• The Director may look at the cube.

• The Director must guide the blindfolded Solver using opposite or misleading verbal instructions (reverse psychology).

• The Solver must continue to follow the Director's instructions.

• The Director must not touch the cube.

• Each team will have 20 minutes to solve the cube.

• The top 3 teams with the shortest solving times will qualify for the Final Round.

 



 

Round 3 – Final Round – Pyraminx Showdown

 

• Each qualifying team will receive a Pyraminx.

• No blindfold will be used in this round.

• Only one member from each team may participate.

• The participating member must be chosen by the team before the round begins.

• Each participant will have 10 minutes to solve the Pyraminx.

• The team whose participating member solves the Pyraminx in the shortest time will be declared the winner of Cube Craze.

 



 

General Rules

 

• The decisions of the organizers will be final and binding.

• Unsportsmanlike behavior, cheating, or any violation of the rules may result in disqualification.

• Participants are expected to follow all instructions given by the event coordinators throughout the competition.

Name of the Event :Argument Arena



Type of Event (Onstage / off Stage) :On Stage



Number of Participants:2(Per Team)



Number of Rounds :3



Rules and Regulations (For each round;if exists) / Guidelines:





Number of Participants: 02 members per team and one team per institution.

Number of Rounds: 03

Rules & Regulations

Team Composition

Two Teams: Each debate consists of two teams—one supporting the topic (For) and the other opposing it (Against). 

Topic and Preparation

Debate Topic: Topics will be given 10 minutes in advance. Lots will be drawn for opponent selection and For/Against. 

An elimination round will be conducted if the number of teams is odd. 

For the elimination round, topics will be given on the spot, and participants must speak on the given topic for 2 minutes. 

Speaking Order and Time Limits

Opening Statements:

For Team: 4 minutes to present their arguments. 

Against Team: 4 minutes to present their counterarguments. 

Response

The Response and Rebuttal Round will be an open-format segment lasting 8 minutes, where both teams may freely engage with and challenge each other’s opening statements.

Participants are encouraged to present counterarguments, clarify positions, and respond directly to points raised by the opposing team.

Closing Statements

Teams will be given 2 minutes each to present their closing statements. 



In Case of an Odd Number of Teams

A presentation round will be conducted in which all teams will present for 2 minutes each on the provided topics. The team with the least points will be eliminated.

Conduct Rules

Respect: Speakers must maintain respect for each other and avoid personal attacks or rude language. 

No Interruptions: Team members should not interrupt the speaker except during the designated response time. 

Fact-check: Use accurate and reliable information to support your argument. 



Judging Criteria (With Points distribution)  : 

Content: Quality, relevance, and depth of the arguments. [10 Points] 

Delivery: Clarity, confidence, and persuasiveness of the speech. [10 Points] 

Rebuttal: Ability to effectively counter the opposing team’s points. [10 Points] 

Team Coordination: How well the team members support each other and present a unified argument. [10 Points] 

Structure: Logical flow and organization of the speech. [10 Points] 

Scoring and Feedback

Points: Judges will score based on the criteria above. 

Tie-Breaker: If there is a tie, an additional round or question may be used to determine the winner. 

Judge’s Decision: The decision of the judges is final and cannot be challenged. 

Penalties

Time Overrun: Exceeding the time limit may result in point deductions. 

Rule Violations: Breach of any rules may lead to penalties or disqualification.

Name of the Event : Relay Tic Tac Toe



Type of Event (Onstage / off Stage) : OFFSTAGE	



Number of Participants: 3 per Higher Secondary



Number of Rounds :2



Rules and Regulations / Guidelines:

Each team consists of 3 players

Each team will be assigned a specific colored marker.

Tournament follows a knockout format.If there is an odd number of teams, one team is chosen by lot to get a Bye (skips the round).

The lot is repeated in later rounds if the number of teams is still odd.

Each match between 2 teams consists of exactly 3 rounds.

Team that wins majority of rounds (best out of 3) wins and advances to the next stage of the bracket.

Position 3 markers in a row (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal).Leave the grid untouched for the referee to check.

False Start: Run only after being tagged.

Touch Opponent's Marker: Round lost.

Disturb Grid: Intentional disturbance - Round lost.



GAME SETUP:

The grid: A 3x3 grid with 9 hoops.

Straight line: A designated straight line approx (20-30 feet) away from grid. Teams stand behind the marked line.

Markers: Each team gets 3 identical markers.

On the whistle, Player 1 runs, places a marker, returns, and tags Player 2.

Player 2 does the same, then tags Player 3.

Player 3 places the last marker and returns.

If no team gets 3 in a row, the next player in rotation (player 1,2,3) continue the game in order.

Players move one of their own markers to an empty spot.

Tag the next player after returning.Continue until a team wins

The Final round will be played on a 4x4 grid. The wining team must make 4 in a row(horizontal, vertical or diagonal).

Name of the Event : Memory Mania



Type of Event : Off Stage 



Number of Participants: 1 per team



Number of Rounds : 03



Round -01 : MATCHING THE CARDS

Objective

The objective of the game is to test the participant’s memory, concentration, and observation skills by identifying and matching pairs of identical cards within the given time limit.



Game Setup

A total of 20 cards will be placed face-down on the table in a predefined arrangement.

The cards will be thoroughly shuffled before the game begins.

Each card will have a matching pair, resulting in 10 pairs in total.

All cards must remain face-down, and participants must not be able to see the patterns before making their selection.



Rules & Regulations

Each participant will be given a fixed time limit to complete the game.

At the start of the game, all 20 cards will be placed face-down.

The participant must select any two cards at a time and turn them over to reveal their patterns.

If the two cards match, the pair will be considered successfully matched and will be removed/kept aside as decided by the organizers.

If the two cards do not match, they must be turned face-down again before the participant proceeds with the next attempt.

Participants must rely on their memory and observation to remember the positions of previously revealed cards.

Participants are not allowed to move, shuffle, or change the position of any card.

Only two cards may be turned over at a time.

Participants must not receive assistance or hints from other participants or spectators.

The game will end when:

The allotted time expires, or

All pairs have been successfully matched, whichever occurs first.

The number of correctly matched pairs will be recorded as the participant’s score.









Scoring & Qualification

1 successfully matched pair = 1 point.

Participants will be ranked according to the number of pairs matched within the given time limit

Participants with the highest scores will qualify for the next round.

The number of participants qualifying for the next round will be decided by the organizers based on the total number of participants.





Tie-Breaker

In case two or more participants obtain the same score, a tie-breaker round may be conducted by the organizers.



Disqualification

A participant may be disqualified for:



Peeking at the cards before the game begins.

Intentionally changing or disturbing the position of the cards.

Taking assistance or hints from others.

Turning over more than two cards at a time.

Engaging in any unfair practice or violating the instructions given by the organizers.



Final Decision

The decision of the game coordinator/judges will be final and binding in case of any dispute or ambiguity.





Round-02: ANALYSE THE IMAGE & SOLVE THE CROSSWORD



Objective

The objective of the game is to test the participant’s observation, memory, concentration, recall, and analytical skills by carefully studying an image and using the information remembered from it to solve a crossword puzzle.



Game Setup

Each participant will be provided with access to a laptop/computer screen.

A specific image containing multiple identifiable elements will be displayed on the screen.

The image will be displayed for 30 seconds only.

After 30 seconds, the image/screens will be turned off or the image will be removed from the participants' view.

A crossword puzzle will then be provided to each participant.

The clues/questions in the crossword will be based on the objects, elements, people, places, symbols, or other details present in the displayed image.



How to Play

The image will be displayed on the participant’s screen for 30 seconds.

Participants must carefully observe and remember as many elements of the image as possible during this time.

Participants may not write down any information while the image is being displayed.

Once the 30 seconds are over, the image will no longer be visible.

The crossword puzzle will then be provided to the participants.

Each crossword clue will relate to an element that was present in the displayed image.

Participants must use their memory and understanding of the image to identify the correct answers.

The answers must be entered in the appropriate boxes of the crossword puzzle.

Participants must complete the crossword within the given time limit.

The completed crossword must be submitted to the event coordinator before the time limit expires.



Rules & Regulations

Participants will get only 30 seconds to observe the image.

The image will be displayed only once and will not be shown again during the round.

Participants are not permitted to take photographs, screenshots, or recordings of the image.

Participants are not allowed to use their phones, the internet, or any external source of information.

No notes or rough work related to the image may be written while the image is being displayed.

Once the image is removed, participants must rely solely on their memory to solve the crossword.

Participants must not communicate or discuss answers with other participants.

Any form of assistance, prompting, or discussion with other participants will be considered a violation of the rules.

Only answers that fit the given clues and crossword structure will be considered valid.

Spelling must be correct. Incorrectly spelled answers will not receive marks.

The crossword must be completed and submitted within the specified time limit.



Scoring

1 correct answer = 1 point.

Points will be awarded only for correctly answered crossword clues.

No negative marking will be applied for incorrect answers.

The participant with the highest score will be ranked highest in the round.







Qualification

Depending on the number of participants, the organizers will decide the number of participants who will proceed to the next round.

Participants will be shortlisted based on their total score and/or completion time, as decided by the organizers before the event.



Tie-Breaker

In case of a tie between participants:



A short additional memory-based question/puzzle may be given as a tie-breaker.

The participant who scores higher in the tie-breaker will qualify.

If required, the organizers may conduct additional tie-breakers until the tie is resolved.



Disqualification

A participant may be disqualified for:



Using a mobile phone, internet, or any unauthorized electronic device.

Taking a photograph or screenshot of the displayed image.

Writing notes while the image is being displayed.

Receiving or providing assistance to another participant.

Discussing answers during the game.

Attempting to access the image after the observation period has ended.

Any other unfair practice as determined by the organizers.



Final Decision

The decision of the game coordinator/judges will be final and binding in case of any dispute, ambiguity, or technical issue during the game.



Round-03: GUESS THE PASSCODE

Objective

The objective of the game is to test the participant’s memory, concentration, observation, recall, logical thinking, and word-solving ability.

Participants must memorize the letters associated with different symbols and later use their memory to identify a hidden word from a given sequence of symbols.







Game Setup

A set of symbols will be displayed on the screen.

Each symbol will be assigned a specific letter.

Participants will be given 1 minute to observe and memorize the symbol–letter associations.

After 1 minute, the symbols and their corresponding letters will be removed from the screen.

Participants will then receive a case/problem statement.

The statement will contain the names of different symbols from the memorization phase in a particular sequence.

Participants must identify the symbols mentioned in the statement and recall the letter associated with each symbol.

The resulting letters will form a jumbled word.

Participants must rearrange the letters and identify the correct meaningful word.





Example Memorization Phase



 Participants are shown:



Symbol

Letter

⭐ Star

T

🔺 Triangle

H

● Circle

I

❤️Heart

N

Diamond

K



The participants get 1 minute to memorize the associations. The display is then removed.

Problem Statement



The participant receives a statement such as:



"During the activity, the Heart, Star, Circle, Diamond and Triangle were observed in the given situation."

The participant must recall:



Heart → N

Star → T

Circle → I

Diamond → K

Triangle → H



The resulting letters are:



N – T – I – K – H 



These letters are jumbled.



The participant must rearrange them to identify the word:



THINK



How to Play

The symbol–letter key will be displayed on the screen for exactly 1 minute.

Participants must carefully observe and memorize the letter associated with each symbol.

Participants are not allowed to write down the symbol–letter combinations during the memorization period.

After 1 minute, the symbol–letter key will be removed.

A problem statement/case will then be provided.

The problem statement will contain the names of several symbols from the memorization phase.

Participants must identify the symbols mentioned in the statement.

Participants must recall the corresponding letters for those symbols.

The recalled letters will form a jumbled sequence.

Participants must rearrange the letters and identify the meaningful word.

The participant who correctly identifies the word first will be declared the winner, subject to verification by the game coordinator.



Rules & Regulations

The symbol–letter key will be displayed only once for 1 minute.

Participants must rely entirely on their memory.

Participants are not allowed to write, photograph, screenshot, or record the displayed information.

Mobile phones, internet access, or any external assistance are strictly prohibited.

Participants must follow the symbols in the exact order in which their names appear in the problem statement.

All the recalled letters must be used to form the final word unless the instructions specifically state otherwise.

Participants must not communicate or discuss the answer with other participants.

Only a meaningful word that matches the intended answer will be considered correct.





Winning Criteria

The winner will be the first participant to correctly identify the hidden word.

The answer must be verified by the game coordinator before the winner is announced.

If the first participant gives an incorrect answer, the opportunity may be given to the next participant, subject to the organizers' decision.



Tie-Breaker

In case of a tie or simultaneous correct answers, an additional symbol–letter decoding challenge will be conducted.

The participant who correctly identifies the word in the shortest time will be declared the winner.



Disqualification

A participant may be disqualified for:



Taking a photograph or screenshot of the symbol–letter key.

Writing down the associations during the memorization period.

Using a mobile phone, internet, or any unauthorized aid.

Taking assistance from another participant.

Communicating the answer to another participant.

Attempting to view the symbol–letter key after it has been removed.

Using any unfair means to obtain the answer.



Final Decision

The decision of the game coordinator/judges will be final and binding in case of any dispute, ambiguity, or disagreement regarding the answer or game procedure.

Name of the Event: Roll Royale

Type of Event (Onstage / Offstage): Onstage

Number of Participants: One participant from each team.

Number of Rounds: Three rounds

Rules and Regulations (for each round, if applicable) / Guidelines:

General Guidelines

1. One participant per team.

2. Participants must report at least 10 minutes before their scheduled match.

3. Participants will be divided into groups of three or four through a draw of lots. No participant will receive a bye.

5. For Rounds 1 and 2, board allocation and playing colour will be decided through a draw of lots. Each lot will mention the team name and the assigned colour.

6. The number of players qualifying from each board in Rounds 1 and 2 will be decided according to the total number of registrations and announced before the event begins.

Standard Ludo Rules

• Each player will have four tokens of one colour: red, blue, green or yellow.

• At the beginning of each match, every player will have one token already placed on the starting square. The remaining tokens may be brought out by rolling a 6.

• To decide who starts, each player will roll the die once. The player who rolls the highest number will begin. In case of a tie for the highest number, the tied players will roll again.

• Play will continue clockwise.

• A token must be moved according to the number rolled on the die.

• Once a token has been moved and released, the move cannot be changed.

• If a player has no valid move, the turn will end.

• Rolling a 6 gives the player one additional turn.

• If a player rolls three consecutive 6s, the turn will end, and the third roll will not be played.

• Tokens placed on safe squares cannot be captured.

• Landing on an opponent's token, unless it is on a safe square, will send that token back to its home area.

• A player who captures an opponent's token will receive one additional turn.

• An exact number is required for a token to enter the home triangle.

• The objective is to move all four tokens from the home area to the home triangle before the other players.

Round 1 - Preliminary Round

• All participants will compete in groups of three or four, formed through a draw of lots.

• Each match will have a time limit of 25 minutes.

• A player who brings all four tokens to the home triangle will secure the highest available qualifying position on that board. Play will continue until the required number of qualifying positions has been decided or the time limit expires.

• The number of players qualifying from each board for Round 2 will be announced before the event begins, based on the total number of participants.

• If the required qualifying positions are not decided within 25 minutes, players will first be ranked according to the number of tokens that have reached the home triangle. If players have the same number of tokens at home, the positions of their remaining tokens will be considered, and the player whose remaining tokens are collectively closest to the home triangle will be ranked higher.

• If a tie affecting qualification remains, an additional five minutes will be given. If the tie still continues, each tied player will roll the die once, and the player with the highest number will qualify. Tied players will roll again until the tie is broken.

Round 2 - Qualifying Round

• The players who qualify from Round 1 will compete in Round 2.

• Participants will again be divided into groups of three or four through a draw of lots. The lot will mention the team name and the assigned colour.

• Each match will have a time limit of 25 minutes.

• The number of players qualifying from each board for Round 3 will be announced before the event begins, based on the total number of participants.

• The same ranking procedure and tie-breaking rules used in Round 1 will apply if the required qualifying positions are not decided within the time limit.

Round 3 - Final Round

• The players who qualify from Round 2 will compete in Round 3, which will be the final round.

• Playing colours will be assigned through a draw of lots before the final begins.

• The final round will have a time limit of 25 minutes.

• The first player to bring all four tokens to the home triangle will be declared the winner.

• If the final is not completed within 25 minutes, players will be ranked according to the number of tokens that have reached the home triangle. If players have the same number of tokens at home, the positions of their remaining tokens will be considered, and the player whose remaining tokens are collectively closest to the home triangle will be ranked higher.

• If a tie remains, an additional five minutes will be given. If the tie still continues, each tied player will roll the die once, and the player with the highest number will be declared the winner. Tied players will roll again until the tie is broken.

Additional Rules

1. A participant who is eliminated from a round will not receive another opportunity to re-enter the competition.

2. No help from teachers, audience members or other participants will be allowed.

3. The organisers' decision will be final and binding in case of any dispute.

Typing Competition – Rules & Regulations

Competition Format

The competition consists of two rounds. Each round carries 10 marks, making a total of 20 marks.



Round 1: Monkey Typing

Description

Participants will be provided with a short and simple text passage to type within the allotted time.

Rules

The duration of this round is 2 minutes. 

Participants must type the given passage as accurately and as quickly as possible. 

Use of the Backspace key is strictly prohibited. 

Spell-check, auto-correct, predictive text, grammar correction, or any similar assistance must be disabled. 

Participants are expected to be familiar with the Monkey Typing format before the competition begins. 

Any use of unauthorised typing assistance or violation of the rules will result in immediate disqualification. 



Round 2: Blind Typing

Description

Participants will be provided with a text passage containing letters, numbers, punctuation marks, and special characters.

Rules

The duration of this round is 2 minutes. 

During typing, the display/monitor will remain blank, and participants will not be able to view the text being typed. 

Participants must rely solely on their typing skills and memory. 

The passage must be typed exactly as provided, including: 

Uppercase and lowercase letters 

Numbers 

Punctuation marks 

Special characters 

Any attempt to bypass the blank screen or use unauthorised tools or techniques will result in immediate disqualification. 





General Rules

Each participant will be given 2 minutes for each round. 

Participants must use only the keyboard provided by the organisers. 

The use of Backspace is strictly prohibited in Round 1. 

Spell-check, auto-correct, predictive text, grammar assistance, macros, or any other typing aid must remain disabled throughout the competition. 

Participants must not use mobile phones, notes, smart devices, or any external assistance during the competition. 

Any attempt to manipulate the system, bypass the blank screen, or use unauthorised software or hardware will result in immediate disqualification. 

Participants are expected to maintain discipline and follow the instructions of the event coordinators at all times. 

Any technical issue must be reported immediately to the event officials. The organisers' decision regarding technical matters shall be final. 

Failure to comply with any of the above rules may lead to disqualification. 



Winner Selection

The combined score from Round 1 and Round 2 (out of 20 marks) will determine the final rankings. 

The top two participants with the highest overall scores will be declared the Winner and Runner-up. 

In the event of a tie, the participant with the higher overall accuracy score will be given preference. If the tie still persists, the judges may conduct a tie-breaker round or decide based on additional criteria determined by the organising committee. 



Decision of the Judges

The decision of the judges and the organising committee shall be final and binding in all matters related to the competition. No requests for re-evaluation or appeals will be entertained.

Name of the Event: Jenga

Type of Event: Off Stage

Number of Participants: 1

Number of Rounds: 2

Rules:



Eligibility: Exactly 1 participant per Higher Secondary School.

Format: Single Elimination (Knockout). Players play 1 vs 1 in pairs. The loser of each match is eliminated; the winner advances to the next round.

Final Round Exception: If more than 2 players reach the Final Round, all remaining finalists play together in a single match, taking turns one after another in a fixed order until only one remains.

Structure: The tower consists of 18 levels with 3 wooden blocks per level (54 blocks total).

Construction: The initial tower setup is done exclusively by the event coordinator before the match starts.

Time Limit: A player has a maximum of 20 seconds to complete their move.

Move Completion: A move is complete only after a block is successfully removed and placed on the top level.

One-Hand Rule: Players must use only one hand to touch, pull, or place a block.

Forbidden Levels: Players cannot pull or remove a block from the top unfinished level.

Top Level Construction: A new level cannot be started until the current top level has a complete set of 3 blocks..

Judging Criteria:

Using Two Hands: Using both hands to touch, pull, steady, or adjust a block will invoke a penalty—your turn is skipped immediately.

Time Violation: Taking longer than 20 seconds to make and complete a move will invoke a penalty—your turn is skipped immediately.

Tower Collapse: If the tower falls during or as a result of your turn, you are eliminated from the game.

1st Place Winner: The single last remaining player after all other competitors have been eliminated.

2nd Place Runner-Up: The player who was eliminated immediately before the 1st Place winner.
